findings.title: AGENTS.md contains UTF-8 mojibake (`â€"` instead of em-dash `—`)
findings.evidence: Line 19 of AGENTS.md (Repo Identity block) had `Minimal static site â€" Aresmax brand landing page` — the byte sequence is CP1252-decoded em-dash that was re-encoded as UTF-8.
findings.impact: Visual corruption in any rendered view (GitHub, IDE, generated docs). Indicator of an inconsistent encoding pipeline that could affect other agency-wide tooling that parses agent manifests.
findings.recommendation: Replace mojibake byte sequence with proper UTF-8 em-dash (—). Audit other repos in the agency for the same artifact.

findings.title: 10 of 11 doc files fail .github/workflows/doc-lint.yml frontmatter schema
standardsBasis: .github/workflows/doc-lint.yml — requires title, owner, status, last_reviewed (and status ∈ {Draft, Active, Review, Deprecated, Archived})
findings.evidence: Python validator embedded in doc-lint.yml requires the four fields. 6 docs had no frontmatter at all; 3 had partial frontmatter with `status: "Current"` which is also not in the VALID set; PRD only missed `last_reviewed`.
findings.impact: Every PR that modifies docs/ would fail the doc-lint job and block merge.
findings.recommendation: Add the canonical 4-field frontmatter to each doc with status=Active and last_reviewed=today.
remediationPlan: Prepend YAML frontmatter to 6 missing files
Upgrade frontmatter in 3 partial files (status invalid)
verificationSteps: Re-run the validator embedded in doc-lint.yml against all docs/**/*.md --> expect 'Frontmatter valid (N files checked)'

findings.title: docs/SECURITY.md misstates the actual Content-Security-Policy
findings.evidence: SECURITY.md claimed `script-src 'self'` and `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`, while index.html line 5 actually declares `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com`. The page also has an inline `<script type="application/ld+json">` block (line 27) that the doc claims does not exist.
findings.impact: Security documentation that contradicts production posture is worse than no documentation — it gives a false sense of control during reviews. A future contributor relying on the doc would over-trust the CSP and could ship an inline-script XSS that the policy does not actually block.
findings.recommendation: Replace the prose claim with the literal CSP. Document each directive's actual value, list the rationale for `'unsafe-inline'` (JSON-LD), and add a Hardening Backlog table.
remediationPlan: Rewrite the Content Security Policy section to mirror the live CSP
Add a Hardening Backlog table with three concrete tightening actions
verificationSteps: diff prose CSP in docs/SECURITY.md vs the meta tag in index.html --> expect zero semantic differences

findings.title: docs/RUNBOOK.md references main branch on a master-default repo
findings.evidence: git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD --> refs/remotes/origin/master. RUNBOOK referenced `git push origin main` and `branch: main` in 4 places.
findings.impact: On-call following the runbook during an incident would attempt to push to a non-existent branch and lose deployment time.
remediationPlan: Edit RUNBOOK.md to use master throughout
verificationSteps: grep -n 'origin main\| main / root\|branch: main' docs/RUNBOOK.md --> expect no matches

findings.title: CSP whitelists unused script source `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com`
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep for cdnjs/cloudflare returns only the CSP whitelist line itself — nothing actually loads from cdnjs.cloudflare.com.
findings.impact: Wider-than-necessary CSP. A future XSS that could inject a script tag would have cdnjs.cloudflare.com as an available payload host.
findings.recommendation: Remove `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com` from script-src. Optionally replace `'unsafe-inline'` with SHA-256 hash of the inline JSON-LD block.
remediationPlan: Edit index.html CSP, drop cdnjs token
